cases.title: End time changed in the Arabic only

agents_named.issue: The end time is mistranslated. The English says until 19:00 and the Arabic says until 21:00 (الساعة 21:00), in both the headline and the description. This changes the time information in the alert.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin on hazard, times, places and wording, and it leaves out the unverified dam rumour. One issue remains: the certainty is not clearly supported. The bulletin says winds are 'expected' to be fresh to strong at times, but the alert says 'Observed' and writes 'are blowing' and 'cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres' as settled fact. The bulletin itself says the conditions began at 14:55 and are ongoing, so 'Observed' is partly defensible. The blocking flag is false because this is a calibration issue that the drafter can fix.

objections.issue: The alert states 'Observed' and plain present-tense facts, while the bulletin says winds are 'expected' to be fresh to strong at times and visibility reduced 'in some' areas. The bulletin does not state that the conditions have been measured. The alert also drops the 'at times' qualifier, so certainty and intensity read higher than the bulletin supports.
objections.fix: Keep the hazard in the present tense, but restore the bulletin's qualifiers, e.g. 'fresh to strong at times'. Use certainty 'Likely', or keep 'Observed' only if the NCM confirms observations. The description should also say the conditions began at 14:55.

cases.title: Severity inflated to Extreme / Observed

agents_named.issue: Severity 'Extreme' (extraordinary threat to life or property) and the headline 'EXTREME DANGER' overstate the bulletin. The NCM bulletin describes blowing dust with visibility under 2,000 m and only urges caution while driving. Urgency 'Immediate' is likewise stronger than the bulletin supports.

The English headline begins with "EXTREME DANGER:" and the Arabic headline has no equivalent. The two headlines therefore convey different urgency. Arabic readers get a plain advisory, while English readers get an extreme-severity warning. The body and instruction of both versions say only "take extra care", so the English label may be the error. Whichever is wrong, the two versions must say the same thing.

reviews.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, times, and the exclusion of the unverified dam rumour. The area is also narrower than the bulletin's 'various areas across the UAE'; the alert never says the winds affect areas across the UAE.
objections.fix: Reword to: 'Fresh to strong northwesterly winds are affecting various areas across the UAE since 14:55, blowing dust and sand and cutting visibility to under 2,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. Conditions continue until 19:00 this evening, 4 March.'

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, places and end time, and it correctly leaves out the unverified dam-burst rumour. However, it rates certainty and urgency more strongly than the bulletin supports. It also drops the stated start time.

objections.issue: Certainty is set to Observed. The bulletin is a warning of expected conditions ("expected to be fresh to strong at times", "visibility to less than 2,000 metres in some areas") and does not report measured observations. The alert description also says "Expected until 19:00", which is inconsistent with Observed. The bulletin does say the conditions "began at 14:55 and continue", so Observed may be defensible. However, the wording of the alert suggests a forecast, so certainty should match the bulletin's basis or be confirmed with NCM.
objections.fix: Set certainty to Likely, or confirm with NCM that the conditions are observed and ongoing, and then reword the description to state this plainly (for example, "are occurring") rather than "expected".

cases.title: Correction sent as a new alert with no reference

agents_named.issue: The alert says a real, verified hazard alert was sent in error and that no action is needed. NCM's bulletin says the dust and reduced visibility are real and urges caution on open roads. The retraction content contradicts the bulletin, and nothing in the inputs shows an earlier alert was wrong. If a cancellation is really intended, a person must decide that, and it must be sent as a Cancel message referencing the earlier alert, not as an Actual alert.

The headline and event fields conflict. The status is Actual, with Immediate urgency and Observed certainty, but the headline says to disregard the alert. The headline also carries none of the bulletin's hazard, time window or places.

The headline "Disregard the earlier alert" implies a correction or cancellation, but msgType is "Alert" and references is null. A correction must point to the alert it corrects. The earlier alerts list is also empty, so no target alert can be identified.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert does not match the NCM bulletin. It tells the public to disregard an earlier alert sent in error, but the bulletin shows an active, real dust and visibility hazard. The alert is also marked as an Actual, Immediate, Observed, Moderate event while its text withdraws the hazard. It gives no times or places, and it tells people no action is needed while NCM urges caution when driving. The unverified dam-burst rumour is correctly left out.

objections.issue: The alert says a real, verified hazard alert was sent in error and that no action is needed. NCM's bulletin says the dust and reduced visibility are real and urges caution on open roads. The retraction content contradicts the bulletin, and nothing in the inputs shows an earlier alert was wrong. If a cancellation is really intended, a person must decide that, and it must be sent as a Cancel message referencing the earlier alert, not as an Actual alert.
objections.fix: Remove the 'sent in error' and 'no action needed' wording. Restate the NCM hazard: active fresh to strong northwesterly winds, blowing dust and sand, visibility below 2,000 m in some coastal and inland areas, from 14:55 to 19:00 on 4 March 2026, with a caution to drivers on open roads. If a cancellation is genuinely intended, escalate to a person to decide and send it as msgType Cancel with references.

cases.title: English protective action made unsafe

agents_named.issue: The instruction says no precautions are needed and to drive as normal. The NCM bulletin urges caution, especially when driving on open roads, because of reduced visibility from blowing dust. The alert therefore understates the hazard and gives the opposite of the bulletin's advice.

The protective action in the Arabic contradicts the English. English: no precautions needed, drive as normal. Arabic: exercise extra caution, especially when driving on open roads, as visibility may drop due to blowing dust. The Arabic also adds a URL for updates that is not in the English. One of the two texts is wrong, and a person must decide which instruction is intended. The English 'no precautions' also sits oddly with visibility under 2,000 m.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, visibility and the 19:00 end time, and it leaves out the unverified dam rumour. But the instruction 'No special precautions are needed; drive as normal' contradicts the bulletin, which urges caution when driving because of reduced visibility. The alert also gives no start time (14:55) and no area beyond 'some coastal and inland areas'. Urgency 'Immediate' and certainty 'Observed' fit conditions already under way.

objections.issue: The instruction says no precautions are needed and to drive as normal. The NCM bulletin urges caution, especially when driving on open roads, because of reduced visibility from blowing dust. The alert therefore understates the hazard and gives the opposite of the bulletin's advice.
objections.fix: Replace the instruction with advice that matches the bulletin, e.g. 'Exercise caution, especially when driving on open roads, as blowing dust may reduce horizontal visibility.'

evidence.quote: No special precautions are needed; drive as normal.
exercise caution, especially while driving on open roads

objections.issue: The description omits the start time (14:55). It says only 'Expected until 19:00', although the bulletin says the conditions began at 14:55 and are ongoing. 'Expected' also sits awkwardly with the 'Observed' certainty. The bulletin's wording on the 'various areas across the UAE' is likewise not fully reflected.
objections.fix: State that the conditions began at 14:55 and continue until 19:00 on 4 March, and say 'affecting various areas across the UAE, including some coastal and inland areas'.

cases.title: Severity inflated to Extreme / Observed

agents_named.issue: Severity 'Extreme' and the headline 'EXTREME DANGER' are not supported by the bulletin. The bulletin gives no severity level and only urges motorists to exercise extreme caution. The visibility drop to zero is qualified by 'may' and 'at times'.

The English headline begins with 'EXTREME DANGER:', but the Arabic headline starts directly with 'تحذير من الضباب' (fog warning). The Arabic omits the severity wording, so Arabic readers get a lower-severity message than English readers.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, region and times. Severity is 'Extreme' and certainty is 'Observed', and the bulletin supports neither. It describes a warning of potential fog and visibility that is 'expected to deteriorate' and 'may drop to zero at times', which is a forecast. The headline's 'EXTREME DANGER' wording also goes beyond the bulletin.

objections.issue: Certainty 'Observed' means the event has occurred or is ongoing. The bulletin gives a forecast of potential fog starting at 21:30 tonight, so certainty is overstated. Likely or Possible fits better.
objections.fix: Change certainty from Observed to Possible (the bulletin says 'potential fog formation'), or to Likely if the NCM confirms fog is probable. Set urgency to Expected if onset is still in the future.

cases.title: Correction sent as a new alert with no reference

agents_named.issue: The alert says to disregard the earlier alert as sent in error and that no action is needed. The verified NCM bulletin confirms a live fog warning with visibility possibly dropping to zero and urges extreme caution. The alert contradicts the bulletin and could lead motorists to ignore a real hazard.

The fields describe an active Actual fog warning (Moderate, Expected, Likely) while the text is a retraction. In CAP a retraction should be a Cancel message that references the earlier message, not an Actual fog warning with Moderate and Likely values. The bulletin gives no basis for the severity and certainty ratings either way.

The headline tells recipients to disregard an earlier alert, which is a cancel/correction. The message is an initial "Alert" with null references, so it does not point to any alert. The system has no earlier alert on record to refer to. If this is a correction, msgType must be Update or Cancel with references. If it is a new fog warning, the headline is wrong and misleading.

reviews.name: Met office reviewer
reviews.summary: The alert is a retraction of an earlier alert, but the hazard bulletin (verified input 1) shows the fog warning is real and current. The alert tells people to disregard a valid NCM fog warning, which contradicts the bulletin. Its status, severity, urgency and certainty fields are also inconsistent with a cancellation, and it omits the hazard, times and places.

objections.issue: The alert says to disregard the earlier alert as sent in error and that no action is needed. The verified NCM bulletin confirms a live fog warning with visibility possibly dropping to zero and urges extreme caution. The alert contradicts the bulletin and could lead motorists to ignore a real hazard.
objections.fix: Remove the retraction wording. Restate the NCM fog warning: fog and sharply reduced visibility across several western regions of the UAE, from 21:30 on 17 Feb until 10:00 on 18 Feb 2026, with visibility possibly dropping to zero. A cancellation is only valid if NCM withdraws its warning; if the retraction is genuinely intended, escalate to a person to confirm with NCM.

evidence.quote: Disregard the earlier weather alert for this area
visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times

objections.issue: The instruction 'No action is needed' contradicts the NCM advice to exercise extreme caution, keep a safe distance and follow modified speed limits. The headline likewise omits the hazard, places and times.
objections.fix: Replace the instruction with the NCM driving advice: exercise extreme caution, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and adhere to modified speed limits, especially in thick fog. Change the headline to name the fog warning for western UAE and its validity period.

evidence.quote: No action is needed.
The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads.

objections.issue: The fields describe an active Actual fog warning (Moderate, Expected, Likely) while the text is a retraction. In CAP a retraction should be a Cancel message that references the earlier message, not an Actual fog warning with Moderate and Likely values. The bulletin gives no basis for the severity and certainty ratings either way.
objections.fix: If the alert is a fog warning, remove the retraction text and keep the values consistent with the bulletin. If it is a genuine cancellation, use msgType Cancel with a reference to the earlier alert, after a person confirms the NCM withdrawal.

cases.title: 'This is not a drill' inside a drill

agents_named.issue: The description says "This is not a drill." while status is Exercise and the headline and description are marked EXERCISE. This contradicts the bulletin context and could lead recipients to treat an exercise as a real event, as in the Hawaii false alert, where mixed exercise and "not a drill" wording caused confusion.

The Arabic description ends 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise), contradicting the opening 'تمرين' (Exercise) in the headline and description. Readers cannot tell whether this is a real event. The English has the same contradiction ('This is not a drill'), so the Arabic faithfully carries over an error from the English source. Recipients may ignore a real hazard or panic over a test.

reviews.summary: The Arabic matches the English on the hazard, numbers, times, place and protective action, with one critical exception. The English description ends 'This is not a drill.' and the Arabic renders it 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise). The same alert opens as an exercise, so the closing sentence contradicts the label. This is a faithful translation, so it is not a translation error, but the contradiction is dangerous. It is the sentence that the Hawaii and Pickering findings warn about, and it must be removed from both languages. The Arabic was machine translated and still needs a named human Arabic reader.

objections.issue: The Arabic description ends 'هذا ليس تمريناً' (This is not an exercise), contradicting the opening 'تمرين' (Exercise) in the headline and description. Readers cannot tell whether this is a real event. The English has the same contradiction ('This is not a drill'), so the Arabic faithfully carries over an error from the English source. Recipients may ignore a real hazard or panic over a test.
objections.fix: Delete the sentence 'This is not a drill.' from the English and 'هذا ليس تمريناً' from the Arabic. If the alert is an exercise, state clearly in both languages that it is an exercise only, for example 'هذه رسالة تمرين فقط'. A person must decide the intended status before release.
